mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5% is interpreted by markets as a signal of tightening financial conditions, which reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5% and remains above for 30 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns over the 60-day horizon are positive in >70% of similar tightening episodes, or the 60-day IC is above 0.05 with p-value < 0.05 in a walk-forward test.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3% for two consecutive months, market expectations of future rate hikes suppress equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 3% and remains above for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: In 10 similar past episodes, the 20-day forward return was non-negative in at least 80% of cases, or the IC is non-negative with p > 0.1.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a strong labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls by more than 0.5 percentage points while PAYEMS increases by 2% in the same month
failure_condition: Over 5 consecutive months with similar labor indicators, the 5-day forward return is negative in more than 50% of periods, or the IC is below -0.1 with p < 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in industrial production (INDPRO) suggests weakening demand for manufactured goods, which reduces growth expectations for the economy and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by 2% in a single month from its prior value
failure_condition: In analogous prior demand contractions, the 20-day forward return was not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the ratio of consumer credit (not directly observable in the catalog, so this sketch is invalid - skip supply) — instead: When the housing starts (not in catalog) — instead: When the ratio of available credit to GDP (not in catalog) — instead: When the S&P 500 itself shows a strong upward momentum (not in catalog) — instead: When the 10-day moving average of new home sales (not in catalog) — instead: Use GDPC1 as a proxy for demand-supply imbalance. A 5-month acceleration in GDPC1 growth signals excess demand, which can support equity valuations and drive positive 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly growth rate exceeds +3% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 10 historical 60-day windows with similar GDPC1 acceleration, the 60-day forward return was not positive in 70% of cases, or IC < 0.02 with p < 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% for 4 consecutive months, without a corresponding rise in labor force participation (PAYEMS), suggests a tight labor market that drives wage growth and corporate profits, producing positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE remains below 3.5% for 4 consecutive months and PAYEMS does not increase by more than 1% in the same period
regime_hint: labor market tightness without participation surge
failure_condition: In 8 comparable labor-tightness episodes, the 20-day forward return was negative in more than half, or the IC is below 0.05 with p < 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp and immediate increase in the federal funds rate above 6% creates immediate discount rate compression, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns within the next 5 days when the move is unexpected.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS jumps by 1 percentage point in a single meeting and is not anticipated in prior months' FOMC statements
failure_condition: In 10 prior surprise hikes, the 5-day forward return was non-negative in more than 60% of cases, or IC > 0.1 with p < 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of industrial production (INDPRO) shows a double dip (consecutive declines), it signals supply-side softness that reduces growth prospects and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO exhibits two consecutive monthly declines in the same quarter
failure_condition: In 15 historical supply weakness episodes, the 20-day forward return was not significantly negative (p > 0.1), or the IC is above 0.05 with p < 0.05.
